title: Newton's Laws - diagnostic quiz
instructions: 8 single-answer questions and 2 short-answer questions. Work individually before group discussion. For Q09-Q10, show your reasoning.

items.stem: A puck slides right at 2.0 m/s on an ideal frictionless horizontal surface. After it is released, the net horizontal force on it is zero. What happens next?
items.hint: Separate an object's current velocity from what changes its velocity.

options.text: It speeds up, then slows down.

items.stem: A 2.0 kg cart is pulled with 10 N to the right while an opposing 4 N force acts to the left. What is its horizontal acceleration?
items.hint: Combine the horizontal forces with signs before dividing by the mass.

items.stem: A 2.0 kg cart and a 4.0 kg cart each experience the same net horizontal force. Compared with the 4.0 kg cart, the acceleration of the 2.0 kg cart is...
items.hint: Think about what mass does to acceleration when the net force is held fixed.

items.stem: A book rests on a table. Which pair is a Newton's third-law force pair?
items.hint: For a third-law pair, ask who exerts each force and which object receives it.

options.text: Earth pulls the book down; the table pushes the book up.
Earth pulls the book down; the book pulls Earth up.
The table pushes the book up; the book has zero acceleration.
The book pushes the table down; Earth pulls the book down.

items.stem: An elevator carries a person upward at a constant speed. Neglect air resistance. What is the scale's upward normal force N on the person?
items.hint: The direction of motion does not by itself establish the direction of acceleration.

items.stem: You push a box horizontally to the right with 12 N. It remains at rest on a rough horizontal floor, and no other horizontal forces act. What is the horizontal static friction force on the box?
items.hint: Use the observed absence of acceleration to balance horizontal forces.

options.text: 0 N, because the box does not move.
The maximum possible static friction, regardless of the push.

items.stem: During a head-on collision, a heavy truck exerts a force on a small car. How does the force exerted by the car on the truck compare at the same instant?
items.hint: Distinguish force magnitude from the resulting acceleration of each object.

options.text: Same magnitude, opposite direction, on the other body.
Smaller magnitude because the car is lighter.
Larger magnitude because the car changes speed more.
Both forces act on the car and cancel.

items.stem: A block is released from rest on a frictionless ramp inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Use g = 9.81 m/s². What is its acceleration along the ramp?
items.hint: Resolve gravity parallel to the slope, rather than using the full weight.

items.stem: A classmate says: "If a cart keeps moving, there must be a force pushing it forward." Explain whether this is correct for a cart moving at constant velocity on an ideal frictionless track. Then explain why everyday carts on rough floors often stop without being pushed.
items.hint: Explain what changes motion and what can simply persist.

items.stem: Two blocks of masses 2.0 kg (A) and 3.0 kg (B) touch on a frictionless horizontal surface. A horizontal 10 N force pushes block A to the right. Find (i) the acceleration of the two-block system, (ii) the contact force of A on B, and (iii) the contact force of B on A. Name which two forces form a third-law pair.
items.hint: First choose both blocks as one system, then isolate block B.
